long_biography.plain_text:
Future computer scientist Jim Clark stood out in algebra during US Navy electronics training and was chosen to teach other students. He took correspondence courses at sea and later attended night classes at Tulane, rebuilding an education interrupted when he left high school. Graduate study eventually took him from physics into computer science.

Clark's philanthropy at Stanford helped establish the Clark Center, which opened in 2003 as a home for the Bio-X programme. The building brought biologists, doctors, chemists, physicists and engineers together to work across disciplinary boundaries. He later pledged additional funding for research combining the life sciences, technology and engineering.
long_biography.html:
Future computer scientist Jim Clark stood out in algebra during US Navy electronics training and was chosen to teach other students. Clark's philanthropy at Stanford helped establish the Clark Center, which opened in 2003 as a home for the Bio-X programme. The building brought biologists, doctors, chemists, physicists and engineers together to work across disciplinary boundaries. He later pledged additional funding for research combining the life sciences, technology and engineering.
